headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors when Great Expectations outputs feed Transformers, with overlapping filesystem writes and broad egress increasing blast radius.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Great Expectations can read and emit validation results and documentation, while Transformers can read/write files and process stdin/stdout. No shared channel is documented by default, so prompt injection is not provable; the only plausible bridge is manual or file-based transfer, which is a low-risk pathway.
conditions: IF operator copies Great Expectations output into a Transformers prompt or script input
IF a shared file is used as an instruction-bearing bridge between the two agents
mitigations: Keep outputs as structured data, not free text
Separate instruction text from validation artifacts
Use a read-only handoff file format
Review any copied content before passing it onward

B_data_leakage.rationale: Great Expectations touches data sources, validation results, and documentation, and Transformers has broad network egress plus file access. A shared workspace or copied artifacts could move sensitive validation data into a networked agent that may transmit context externally. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default workflows, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Great Expectations writes validation results into a workspace readable by Transformers
IF Transformers processes those files while network egress remains enabled
mitigations: Store validation outputs in a restricted directory
Disable network egress for the Transformers run
Redact sensitive columns before handoff
Use separate service accounts or containers
Delete transient artifacts after processing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Great Expectations writes validation results and documentation, and Transformers can read and write the filesystem, execute shell, and spawn subprocesses. Both can mutate shared files, so concurrent runs can overwrite model files, scripts, or reports. Because Transformers supports multiple instances and no locking is documented, the conflict is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same writable directory
IF either agent modifies shared model files, scripts, or reports without external locking
mitigations: Run each agent in its own directory
Make shared inputs read-only
Add a simple lock file around writes
Snapshot the workspace before concurrent runs
Use separate containers or users

D_cascading_error.rationale: Great Expectations produces validation results that Transformers can ingest through files or stdin/stdout. If Transformers treats those outputs as authoritative, errors or malformed assertions can cascade into downstream text generation or scripts. The pair is not documented as a verified pipeline, so this is inferred, but the default file-based handoff makes the risk real.
conditions: IF Transformers consumes Great Expectations validation output without an explicit verification step
IF downstream actions are generated from those outputs
mitigations: Require a human review step before acting
Validate schema and provenance of handoff files
Separate facts from recommendations in the output format
Reject malformed or partial validation records

E_compliance.rationale: Great Expectations handles data quality tests and validation results, while Transformers processes text, images, audio, video, and multimodal data with broad egress. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so compliance risk is limited to documented gaps in handling the same data classes rather than a clear violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is included in validation results or multimodal inputs
IF the deployment requires residency or retention controls not enforced by the workspace
mitigations: Classify data before processing
Apply retention limits to shared artifacts
Route regulated data through a compliant environment
Log access to validation outputs
Review vendor terms for the specific deployment
